quotes.quote: Artists and their teams can use the Bandsintown API to display event data on their website or app. The Bandsintown API is designed for artists looking to promote their shows on their websites with full control over the rendering of events.
Managers can get their own API Key to access the API through Bandsintown for Artists ... PLEASE NOTE: Each API Key is linked to a single artist unless authorized otherwise by Bandsintown.
PLEASE NOTE: The data is not meant to be used in any other circumstances unless specifically approved by Bandsintown. Review our Terms & Conditions.

Access to our API is available for organizations looking to integrate Bandsintown data into their platforms or services through our partnership program. If your organization is interested in leveraging our data applications, please contact us to discuss partnership opportunities and the applicable terms.
How to get artist information — By Artist Name: https://rest.bandsintown.com/artists/{{artist_name}}/?app_id=... By Artist ID ... By Facebook page ID ...

Our API can return two different results: 1. Artist information ... 2. Artist events: returns the list of events including their date and time, venue name and location, ticket links, lineup, description, title, and the link to the Bandsintown event page

apiTerms.summary: Bandsintown's API is built for a single artist's own site/app to show THAT artist's events — you get an app_id tied to one artist via 'Bandsintown for Artists' (the manager/artist account), and Bandsintown explicitly says the data 'is not meant to be used in any other circumstances unless specifically approved.' There's no city-level query — every documented endpoint is keyed by artist_name/artist_id/Facebook page id (never by location), so a fan app that wants 'what's coming to Austin' can't ask that question at all even with a legitimate key; you'd have to hold one app_id per artist you care about and filter events client-side by venue city. A personal, non-commercial multi-artist fan app does NOT fit the documented free path (one key = one artist, needs a Bandsintown-for-Artists account which is meant for the artist/their manager) — building 'MUNA-style alert for any artist in Austin' on the official API would mean either (a) requesting one app_id per followed artist by claiming to represent each one (against the stated terms), or (b) going through Bandsintown's partnership/contact-us program for broader multi-artist or city-based access, which is a business conversation, not a self-serve signup. No caching/display rules are spelled out on these pages beyond 'full control over the rendering of events' and the general data-use restriction; the actual Terms & Conditions doc (corp.bandsintown.com/data-applications-terms) was not fetched in this pass — worth pulling if a real integration decision hinges on caching/redistribution rules.
